name: Kumararama (Kumara Bhimeswara Temple)
deity: The presiding deity is Kumara Bhimeswara Swamy, a form of Shiva worshipped as a tall white lingam. His consort here is revered as Bala Tripura Sundari.
summary: Kumararama at Samalkota is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras of coastal Andhra, dedicated to Shiva as Kumara Bhimeswara. It is distinguished by a two-storeyed sanctum housing an unusually tall lingam and by a large walled complex with a soaring gopuram. The site is also known as Bhimarama.

sections.history: Kumararama is traditionally credited to the Eastern Chalukya king Chalukya Bhima I, who reigned in the early tenth century, and the temple carries his name in the deity's title. The Eastern Chalukyas ruled the deltaic country between the Godavari and Krishna rivers from Vengi, and their patronage shaped several important shrines of the region. Inscriptions associated with the complex record grants and later additions by successive rulers and patrons. Over the centuries the temple was maintained and repaired, with a tall enclosing wall and gateway giving it the character of a fortified sacred precinct. As one of the five Pancharama shrines, it has long drawn pilgrims travelling the wider circuit across the Andhra deltas.
sections.architecture: The temple is built to a plan unusual among the Pancharama shrines: the sanctum rises through two storeys, and the white lingam is so tall that its upper portion is venerated from a raised gallery on the second level. The main shrine stands within a spacious walled enclosure entered through a tall, tiered gopuram. Stone pillars, some carrying carved detail, support the mandapas leading toward the sanctum, and the fabric reflects Eastern Chalukya practice with later accretions. A temple tank is associated with the site, in keeping with the region's sacred landscape. The scale of the enclosure and the height of the lingam together give the complex its distinctive presence.
sections.legends: The Pancharama legend traces the five shrines to a single great lingam once worshipped by the demon Tarakasura, which broke into pieces during his defeat. Each fragment is said to have come to rest at one of the five sites and to have been established there by a different divine figure. At Samalkota the installation and worship are attributed to Kumara Swamy, the youthful war-god also known as Kartikeya or Subrahmanya, from whom the shrine takes the name Kumararama. Because the fragments retained the power of continued growth, the lingam here is remembered as rising ever taller, an explanation devotees offer for its striking height and the two-storeyed sanctum built to honour it.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri is the foremost observance at Kumararama, drawing large gatherings for night-long worship and the celebration of Kalyanotsavam, the ceremonial marriage of the deities. The month of Karthika, sacred to Shiva, brings sustained devotion with lamp-lighting and special abhishekams. Devi Navaratri is observed for the goddess Bala Tripura Sundari with daily rituals and adornment. Through these seasons the walled complex fills with pilgrims of the Pancharama circuit, and the temple keeps to the rhythms of the traditional festival calendar. Visitors planning to attend a particular festival should confirm dates and timings with the temple beforehand, as these follow the lunar calendar.
sections.experience: A visit begins at the tall gopuram, which opens from the town into the wide, quiet enclosure. Within, the two-storeyed sanctum invites an unusual sequence of worship: devotees offer prayers at ground level and then ascend to view and venerate the upper part of the tall lingam. The scale of the walled precinct lends a measured, unhurried atmosphere, and the temple tank adds to the sense of a self-contained sacred space. Mornings and evenings, framed by ritual and lamp-light, are the most atmospheric times to be present. For those following the Pancharama route, Kumararama offers both a distinctive form of darshan and a moment of calm within a historic setting.

visit.timings: The temple generally opens in the early morning and again in the evening, with a midday closure, following the customary pattern for the region. Exact hours vary by season and festival, so verify locally before travelling.
visit.dressCode: Modest, traditional attire is expected. Visitors typically remove footwear before entering the inner precinct; covering the shoulders and legs is advisable.
visit.photography: Photography rules vary and are often restricted within the sanctum. Seek permission and follow the temple staff's guidance, especially near the shrine.
visit.gettingThere: Samalkota is a railway junction on the Howrah–Chennai line, well connected by train. It lies close to Kakinada and Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram); the nearest airport is at Rajahmundry, and buses and taxis serve the town.
